chapter: Sue and Patsy Howard in show business
title: Cee Pee Johnson and Mickey Cohen
summary: Collette and Patsy tell how Cee Pee Johnson walked off the bandstand and Cohen coaxed him back.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I know it was very scary, because Cee Pee Johnson they came upstairs where we were and the (inaudible) but Mickey took a gun and threatened him to go down and play, and Cee Pee was fixing his hair --
I don't know what night it was --
And he just went on like he didn't and he didn't hit him. It's almost like he see the man (inaudible) you know we'll play when you want to. Cee Pee
You see, C.P., he had said that this
particular night, he walked off the bandstand and Mickey Cohen came up to find out what was wrong.

Right, and he said 'I can't satisfy you. One minute I play too loud and the next minute you tell me I play too soft, and Cee Pee had always said what he would do if they threatened him or anything, so I never will forget we were watching from our dressing room and Mickey Cohen came up with this soft voice and his henchmen, and he said, Cee Pee what's the matter, and Cee Pee said I'm just tired of being pushed around like this, I can't satisfy anybody, so I am going to quit and he said, aw, Cee Pee, don't do that.' And Cee Pee said 'Yes, I'm quitting and started packing up,' So he told him he'd give him three minutes to get back on' the bandstand. He was something else.
Did you realize when you were standing up your rights, that it might be dangerous?
Certainly, but you know, in a fit of anger, you don't care, especially when there's money involved.
I know a few years later than that, Mickey Cohen was supposed to be the head of things of the underworld. here.
Yes, but then he went to prison.
